items.rationale: The bicycle was recovered undamaged. Sections 2.3.3 and 7.1.8(c) exclude the entire elective frame swap, not just the premium over a standard frame.
The brakes were replaced as part of routine servicing, not to repair theft damage, so §§3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude the full line.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(a) exclude routine servicing and tuning in full.
Under §7.1.10, shipping for the excluded shop work is also excluded; no portion is identified as transport from the recovery site under §5.2.2(d).
Sections 7.1.8(f) and 7.1.10 exclude attendance charges on the bicycle-shop invoice because none of its work is covered.
Under §§3.1.6 and 7.1.10, assembly follows the excluded upgrade and service work it supports.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude labour of every grade on the elective upgrade and routine service.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude skilled labour on the elective upgrade and routine service just as they exclude the underlying work.

Section 5.2.2(a) covers necessary attendance to recover the bicycle even though it was undamaged, assuming scheduled off-premises theft cover. Estimated recovery costs are below both the €1,000 recovery limit and the €500 mobility limit; no deductible amount is stated.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers cutting and removal necessary to free the bicycle. Allow €100 gross for the two recorded units together, without treating them as two separate lock releases or counting the separately billed labour twice under §7.1.8(g).

Section 5.2.2(b) covers an hour of necessary locksmith labour at about €40 gross if it is distinct from the cutting charge; §7.1.8(g) excludes any duplicate. The aggregate mobility limit does not reduce the estimate.
